title: 'No other option': Excerpts of Putin's speech declaring war
claim: Putin framed the February 24 invasion as a necessary security move, warned that a direct attack on Russia would bring catastrophic consequences, and said Ukraine should not be allowed to acquire nuclear weapons.
source_confidence_reason: Direct transcript excerpt published the day of the invasion, translated from the Kremlin recording.
ruler_attribution: Directly attributed to Putin as the speaking president.
contrary_evidence: The speech is self-justifying propaganda, not an independent account of the war's causes.

title: General Assembly Overwhelmingly Adopts Resolution Demanding Russian Federation Immediately End Illegal Use of Force in Ukraine, Withdraw All Troops
claim: The UN General Assembly demanded that Russia immediately end its invasion, withdraw all forces from Ukraine, and stop further use or threat of force.
source_confidence_reason: Official UN meeting coverage summarizing the adopted resolution and vote.
period_fit: Directly in-period, days after the invasion.
ruler_attribution: Attributes the invasion and ongoing use of force to the Russian state under Putin.
contrary_evidence: Russia voted against the resolution and argued its actions were defensive.

title: Путин поручил Минобороны РФ обеспечить поддержание мира в ДНР и ЛНР
claim: Putin's recognition decrees for the self-proclaimed DPR and LPR said Ukraine had refused peaceful settlement under the Minsk agreements and ordered the Russian military to perform peacekeeping functions there.
source_confidence_reason: Russian-language publication of the decree text on the day it was signed.
ruler_attribution: Direct presidential decree attributable to Putin.
contrary_evidence: The decrees were widely treated internationally as a prelude to aggression rather than peacekeeping.

title: Russia reframes war goals as Ukrainians advance near Kyiv
claim: Reuters reported that Moscow was scaling back its ambitions in Ukraine after setbacks near Kyiv and shifting focus to the eastern Donbass region.
source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous Reuters reporting on the Russian side's change in stated military aims.
ruler_attribution: Reflects Putin's war policy as implemented by the Russian state.
contrary_evidence: The article describes a military adjustment after failure, not a genuine peace settlement.

title: Ukraine offers neutrality in exchange for NATO-style security guarantees at Russia talks
claim: At the Istanbul talks, Ukraine proposed neutrality in exchange for security guarantees and a ceasefire, showing a plausible diplomatic alternative existed in March 2022.
source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous Reuters report quoting the Ukrainian negotiating position.
ruler_attribution: Provides the alternative Putin could have negotiated toward or rejected.
contrary_evidence: This source shows the alternative existed; it does not prove Putin accepted it.

title: Итоги российско-украинских переговоров в Стамбуле. Главное
claim: Kommersant reported that Russia said it would reduce military activity on the Kyiv and Chernihiv fronts after the Istanbul talks and had received Ukrainian written proposals on neutrality and security guarantees.
source_confidence_reason: Russian-language contemporaneous summary of the talks and Russian claims about de-escalation.
period_fit: Directly in the March 2022 negotiation window.
ruler_attribution: Attributable to the Russian negotiating position under Putin.
contrary_evidence: The reduction was framed as conditional and reversible, not a durable ceasefire.

title: Ukraine: Amid mounting human cost, parties must uphold international humanitarian law
claim: The ICRC warned that parties must spare civilians and immediately allow safe passage for people fleeing the fighting.
source_confidence_reason: Direct ICRC statement during the first week of the full-scale war.
period_fit: Very strong fit to early-war civilian-protection duties in 2022.
ruler_attribution: Applies to the Russian side as a party controlling the invasion.
contrary_evidence: The statement is general to parties, not a Putin-only finding.

title: Ukraine: As humanitarian crisis deepens, parties urgently need to agree on concrete measures; misinformation risks lives
claim: The ICRC said the parties were still failing to meet core humanitarian obligations and that misinformation was harming humanitarian operations.
source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous ICRC field statement with direct operational relevance.
ruler_attribution: The critique applies to Russian conduct as a principal belligerent.
contrary_evidence: It addresses both parties, though Russia was the main aggressor in the conflict.

title: Ukraine: "Level of death, destruction and misery abhorrent and unacceptable"
claim: The ICRC described the level of civilian suffering in Ukraine as abhorrent and unacceptable and emphasized that IHL is about how warfare is conducted, not justifications for war.
source_confidence_reason: Formal ICRC statement linking civilian harm and conduct obligations.
ruler_attribution: Relevant to the Russian invasion and occupation conduct under Putin.
contrary_evidence: The statement does not allocate all responsibility to one side in that paragraph.

title: Russia-Ukraine: Civilian lives and infrastructure must be protected
claim: The ICRC warned that explosive weapons in populated areas were endangering civilians and damaging essential infrastructure such as power and water systems.
source_confidence_reason: Direct October 2022 humanitarian warning tied to the war's destructive pattern.
ruler_attribution: Applies to Russian military operations ordered under Putin.
contrary_evidence: The warning is general, not a command-chain finding.

title: Death and defiance in a Bucha neighbourhood that was held by Russian troops
claim: Reuters described dead civilians and mutilated bodies in Bucha after Russian troops occupied the area, reinforcing the scale of civilian harm during the invasion.
source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous Reuters field report from a major evidence site.
ruler_attribution: The occupation was carried out by Russian forces under Putin's war.
contrary_evidence: The article is a local field account, not a legal judgment.

title: At least 30 civilians killed in Russian strike on convoy, Ukraine says
claim: Reuters reported a missile strike on a civilian convoy in Zaporizhzhia that killed at least 30 civilians and injured nearly 100.
source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous Reuters casualty report from an attack on civilians.
ruler_attribution: The strike is attributed to Russian forces in Ukraine under Putin's command structure.
contrary_evidence: Ukraine reported the attack, and Reuters could not independently verify the exact perpetrator at publication time.

title: U.S. issues new Russia sanctions for annexations in Ukraine; targets firms, lawmakers
claim: Reuters reported that Putin proclaimed Russia's rule over about 15% of Ukrainian territory after the annexation move, prompting U.S. sanctions.
source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous Reuters reporting on the annexation and its international reaction.
ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Putin's territorial escalation.
contrary_evidence: Russia treated the move as lawful reunification; most states rejected it as illegal annexation.

title: UN Commission has found an array of war crimes, violations of human rights and international humanitarian law have been committed in Ukraine
claim: The UN Commission found reasonable grounds to conclude that war crimes and serious human-rights and IHL violations had been committed in Ukraine, with Russian armed forces responsible for the vast majority of violations identified.
source_confidence_reason: Official UN commission summary of a detailed report to the General Assembly.
period_fit: Covers the February-March 2022 phase of the war and its findings were published in 2022.
ruler_attribution: The findings concern Russian armed forces operating under Putin's war policy.
contrary_evidence: The commission also noted some Ukrainian violations in a smaller number of cases.

title: Update on the human rights situation in Ukraine, 24 February – 26 March 2022
publisher: UN Human Rights Monitoring Mission in Ukraine
claim: OHCHR said the Russian Federation launched an armed attack on Ukraine and that hostilities used wide-area explosive weapons in populated areas, causing at least 2,909 civilian casualties by 26 March 2022.
source_confidence_reason: Primary UN human-rights monitoring report written during the conflict.
period_fit: Excellent fit to the opening month of the war.
ruler_attribution: Directly linked to the Russian armed attack ordered under Putin.
contrary_evidence: The update notes some allegations against Ukrainian forces as well.

title: UN report details summary executions of civilians by Russian troops in northern Ukraine from February to April
publisher: UN Human Rights Monitoring Mission in Ukraine
claim: OHCHR reported that Russian troops killed hundreds of civilians in northern Ukraine, including documented summary executions in Bucha and other locations.
source_confidence_reason: Later 2022 UN human-rights report with concrete casualty and method findings.
ruler_attribution: Russian troops were operating under Putin's command in the invasion.
contrary_evidence: The report says some allegations were still being corroborated, so totals are conservative.

title: Russia commits indiscriminate attacks during the invasion of Ukraine
claim: Amnesty said the Russian invasion was marked by indiscriminate attacks on civilian areas and protected objects such as hospitals, and that the Russian government should take responsibility.
source_confidence_reason: Immediate independent field research published two days after the invasion.
ruler_attribution: The attacks were carried out by Russian forces in Putin's invasion.
contrary_evidence: Amnesty's conclusion is rights-based and does not itself determine criminal liability.

title: Ukraine: Russian forces extrajudicially executing civilians in apparent war crimes – new testimony
claim: Amnesty said Russian forces extrajudicially executed civilians in Ukraine and committed other unlawful killings in the Kyiv region.
source_confidence_reason: Detailed eyewitness-based investigation from the occupation zone.
period_fit: Directly covers the March-April 2022 occupation period.
ruler_attribution: Attributable to Russian forces under Putin's wartime command.
contrary_evidence: The report is an investigative allegation pending formal prosecution, not a court verdict.

title: Ukraine: Russian forces must face justice for war crimes in Kyiv Oblast – new investigation
claim: Amnesty documented unlawful air strikes and extrajudicial executions in towns northwest of Kyiv and said civilian deaths included at least 40 people in Borodyanka and 22 unlawful killings in Bucha and nearby towns.
source_confidence_reason: Strong investigative report with multiple interviews and material evidence.
ruler_attribution: Russian forces acting under Putin's invasion policy.
contrary_evidence: Amnesty says the findings should be used to preserve evidence for future prosecutions.

title: Ukraine: “Anyone can die at any time”: Indiscriminate attacks by Russian forces in Kharkiv, Ukraine
claim: Amnesty found that Russian forces carried out a relentless campaign of indiscriminate bombardment in Kharkiv, shelling residential neighborhoods and using cluster munitions.
source_confidence_reason: Focused 2022 report based on on-the-ground investigation and technical evidence.
period_fit: Covers February-June 2022 bombardment of a major city.
ruler_attribution: Russian forces were the attacking party in Putin's war.
contrary_evidence: The report is specific to Kharkiv and does not cover the entire war theater.

title: Ukraine: “Like A Prison Convoy”: Russia’s Unlawful Transfer And Abuse of Civilians In Ukraine During ‘Filtration’
claim: Amnesty found that Russian and Russian-controlled forces unlawfully transferred or deported civilians from occupied parts of Ukraine and subjected them to abusive filtration procedures.
source_confidence_reason: Detailed 2022 investigative report with a direct summary finding.
period_fit: Late-2022 occupation governance and civilian transfer practices.
ruler_attribution: Applies to Russian-controlled structures operating under Putin's occupation policy.
contrary_evidence: The report includes Russian-controlled forces, not only Moscow-commanded regular troops.

title: Ukraine: Apparent War Crimes in Russia-Controlled Areas
claim: HRW documented summary executions, rape, threats, and other grave abuses by Russian military forces in occupied areas of Kyiv, Chernihiv, and Kharkiv regions.
source_confidence_reason: Major rights-group report with specific locations, dates, and victims.
ruler_attribution: Russian military forces were acting under Putin's invasion and occupation orders.
contrary_evidence: HRW uses the phrase apparent war crimes; it is not a court judgment.

title: Ukraine | International Criminal Court
claim: The ICC opened an investigation into the situation in Ukraine on 2 March 2022, and the page later states there are reasonable grounds to believe Putin bears responsibility for unlawful deportation and transfer of children from occupied areas of Ukraine.
locator: situation overview and Putin suspect section
source_confidence_reason: Official court page summarizing the investigation and suspect determinations.
period_fit: The investigation began in 2022 and concerns conduct from 24 February 2022 onward.
ruler_attribution: Directly names Putin in the suspect section.
contrary_evidence: The arrest-warrant findings were issued later, in 2023, even though they concern 2022 conduct.

title: Exclusive-As war began, Putin rejected a Ukraine peace deal recommended by his aide: sources
claim: Reuters reported that Putin's chief envoy on Ukraine told him a provisional deal with Kyiv would satisfy Russia's demand that Ukraine stay out of NATO, but Putin rejected it, expanded objectives toward annexing Ukrainian territory, and pressed ahead with the military campaign.
source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous Reuters reporting based on sources close to the Russian leadership; the Kremlin denied it, so attribution is strong but not independently documented.
ruler_attribution: High: the decision is explicitly attributed to Putin by sources close to his leadership and concerns his choice over available peace terms.
contrary_evidence: Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said the report had no relation to reality
A Ukrainian adviser said Russia was never interested in a peaceful settlement

title: Russia: 'Filtration' of Ukrainian civilians a 'shocking violation' of people forced to flee war
claim: Amnesty said Russian soldiers subjected Ukrainian civilians to abusive filtration, many displaced people reached Russia or Russian-occupied territory involuntarily, and vulnerable groups including children, older people, and people with disabilities were blocked or constrained from fleeing.
source_confidence_reason: Direct Amnesty field reporting contemporaneous with the occupation; strong on the mechanism and victim groups, though based on interviews and UN verification rather than Russian admission.
ruler_attribution: High: the abusive screening and transfer regime operated in Russian-occupied territory under Russian military control.
contrary_evidence: Russia portrayed movements as evacuations or temporary placement rather than forced transfer

title: Доповідь ООН описує свавільні страти та напади на окремих цивільних осіб із боку російських військ на півночі України з лютого до квітня
publisher: Моніторингова місія ООН з прав людини в Україні
claim: The UN human-rights mission said Russian armed forces arbitrarily executed or attacked civilians in the early weeks of the invasion, causing hundreds of civilian deaths in Kyiv, Chernihiv, and Sumy oblasts between 24 February and 6 April 2022.
source_confidence_reason: Official UN monitoring report with concrete casualty totals and time/place bounds; strong independent corroboration of unlawful conduct.
period_fit: Directly in-period, February-April 2022, reported in December 2022.
ruler_attribution: High: the conduct is attributed to Russian troops acting under Putin's wartime command authority.
contrary_evidence: Russia disputed blame for civilian deaths and denied unlawful targeting

title: The Secretary-General - remarks to press on Russian decision on annexation of Ukrainian territory
claim: The UN Secretary-General said the Kremlin's planned annexation of Donetsk, Luhansk, Kherson, and Zaporizhzhia would have no legal value, the referenda were held under occupation during active armed conflict, and the move would further jeopardize peace prospects.
source_confidence_reason: Direct UN statement on the legal status and peace implications of the annexation process, contemporaneous and specific.
ruler_attribution: High: it addresses a Kremlin-announced annexation process driven by Putin's government.
contrary_evidence: Russia treated the referenda as legitimate and the annexations as lawful

title: Recent challenges to security in Europe: what role for the Council of Europe?
publisher: Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe
claim: PACE declared that the Russian Federation's unprovoked and unjustified war of aggression against Ukraine, waged in open defiance of international law, had gravely harmed the international order and unsettled the European multilateral architecture.
source_confidence_reason: Formal adopted resolution of the Council of Europe, a strong legal-political record of international condemnation.
ruler_attribution: Moderate to high: the resolution concerns Russia's war of aggression under Putin's command, though it is an institutional finding rather than a transcript of his private decision.
contrary_evidence: Russia rejected the characterization as aggression and argued its actions were defensive

title: Council of Europe suspends Russia's rights of representation
claim: The Council of Europe suspended the Russian Federation from its rights of representation because of its armed attack on Ukraine.
source_confidence_reason: Official institutional action taken immediately after the invasion; strong for the international reaction to Russia's conduct.
ruler_attribution: Moderate: this is an institutional sanction in response to Putin's attack, not a first-hand record of a secret decision.
contrary_evidence: Russia maintained that its military action was legitimate self-defense

title: Putin says Russia ready to negotiate over Ukraine, Kyiv voices doubts
claim: Putin said Russia was open to negotiations over the war in Ukraine, but the report noted he blamed Kyiv and Western backers for the lack of talks, demanded terms that would require Ukraine to accept Russia's annexation claims, and cited Washington's view that this was posturing amid persistent Russian attacks.
source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous Reuters reporting on a direct Putin statement, with immediate U.S. and Ukrainian pushback; strong for the claim and its contested credibility.
ruler_attribution: High: the quote is directly Putin's, but it is a conditional negotiation stance on terms he controlled.
contrary_evidence: U.S. State Department called it posturing
Ukraine said Russia did not want talks

title: Allegations of Genocide under the Convention on the Prevention and Punishment of the Crime of Genocide (Ukraine v. Russian Federation), Order of 16 March 2022
claim: The ICJ found Ukraine had a plausible right not to be subjected to Russian military operations under the claimed genocide-prevention rationale and ordered Russia to immediately suspend the military operations it commenced on 24 February 2022.
source_confidence_reason: Primary international court order with direct legal findings and binding provisional measures.
ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Putin's launched invasion and Russia's wartime justification for it.
contrary_evidence: Russia disputed the court's framing and the order did not reach the merits of the case.

title: Security Council Calls Emergency Special Session of General Assembly on Ukraine Crisis, Adopting Resolution 2623 (2022) by 11 Votes in Favour, 1 Against, 3 Abstentions
claim: The Security Council, after Russia voted against resolution 2623, called an emergency special session of the General Assembly on the Ukraine crisis because the Council's permanent members lacked unanimity on Russia's actions.
source_confidence_reason: Official UN Security Council press release summarizing a recorded vote and its procedural consequence.
ruler_attribution: Russia's veto role is directly attributable to Putin's government as the permanent member represented in the Council.
contrary_evidence: The result is procedural rather than a merits ruling, so it primarily shows obstruction of UN peace action rather than a substantive judgment.

title: General Assembly Overwhelmingly Adopts Resolution Demanding Russian Federation Immediately End Illegal Use of Force in Ukraine, Withdraw All Troops
claim: The General Assembly demanded that Russia immediately end its invasion of Ukraine, unconditionally withdraw all forces, reverse its February 21 decision on the Donetsk and Luhansk regions, and allow humanitarian access and civilian protection.
source_confidence_reason: Official UN General Assembly press release summarizing the adopted resolution and vote.
ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Putin's invasion and subsequent escalation posture.
contrary_evidence: The resolution was nonbinding, so it is evidence of international rejection rather than enforced compliance.

title: With 143 Votes in Favour, 5 Against, General Assembly Adopts Resolution Condemning Russian Federation’s Annexation of Four Eastern Ukraine Regions
claim: The General Assembly condemned Russia's attempted annexation of Donetsk, Kherson, Luhansk, and Zaporizhzhia and demanded that Russia immediately withdraw and reverse those decisions.
source_confidence_reason: Official UN General Assembly press release on a recorded vote and resolution text.
ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Putin's annexation decisions.
contrary_evidence: The resolution is nonbinding, but it remains strong evidence of international legal and political repudiation.

title: General Assembly Adopts Text Recommending Creation of Register to Document Damages Caused by Russian Federation Aggression against Ukraine, Resuming Emergency Special Session
claim: The General Assembly recommended creating an international damage register and recognized the need for accountability and reparations for damage caused by Russia's wrongful acts in Ukraine.
source_confidence_reason: Official UN General Assembly press release summarizing the adopted text and vote.
ruler_attribution: Attributable to Putin's war and annexation policy as the underlying conduct being addressed.
contrary_evidence: The vote concerns accountability after the fact rather than a direct contemporaneous change in conduct.

title: Exclusive-As war began, Putin rejected a Ukraine peace deal recommended by his aide: sources
claim: Reuters reported that Putin rejected a provisional deal recommended by his envoy Dmitry Kozak that would have removed the need for large-scale occupation, and instead expanded Russia's objectives to include annexation of Ukrainian territory.
locator: opening paragraphs and later summary of Kozak talks
source_confidence_reason: Reuters exclusive based on multiple anonymous sources close to the Russian leadership; credible but not independently document-verified.
period_fit: Target-period 2022 with retrospective reporting on the invasion period.
ruler_attribution: Directly attributed to Putin's rejection of a negotiated off-ramp.
contrary_evidence: Kremlin denied the report and Ukraine did not confirm the proposed deal.

title: Joint Coordination Centre opens in Istanbul to facilitate safe export of commercial foodstuffs and fertilizers from Ukrainian ports
claim: Russia, Ukraine, Türkiye, and the UN inaugurated a Joint Coordination Centre in Istanbul to operationalize the Black Sea Grain Initiative and establish a humanitarian maritime corridor for safe exports of grain, foodstuffs, and fertilizers.
source_confidence_reason: Primary UN press release with concrete implementation details, named participants, and a clear humanitarian purpose.
ruler_attribution: Attributable to Putin's government through Russia's direct participation in the agreement and JCC implementation.
contrary_evidence: The initiative was a limited humanitarian corridor, not a general shift away from the broader war.
